speaker: Doctor
text: I will ask you a few questions to understand your painful, ulcerative skin lesion on your leg. Can you describe when the lesion first appeared and how it has changed since then?

speaker: Patient
text: 54-year-old woman. The patient reports a skin lesion on her right leg that has been present for 1 month. The lesion began as a small red spot and has increased in size. She recalls an ant bite at the site before the lesion developed. She has a history of anterior uveitis treated with corticosteroids 8 months ago, as well as Crohn's disease, type 2 diabetes mellitus, and hypertension.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Pyoderma Gangrenosum.

The patient is a 54-year-old woman with significant comorbidities (Crohn's disease, diabetes) presenting with a one-month history of a painful, enlarging ulcerative lesion on her right leg, which she attributes to a recent ant bite. Given her underlying inflammatory conditions, this clinical picture is highly suggestive of pyoderma gangrenosum rather than an infectious etiology.
